name: Renegade Row
description: The renegade row combines a plank position with a unilateral dumbbell row, performed with both hands gripping dumbbells on the floor in a push-up stance. The movement demands simultaneous anti-rotation core stability, pushing muscle endurance in the support arm and pressing muscles, and pulling strength in the rowing arm. It is a highly efficient full-body exercise that trains the back, core, and shoulder stabilizers in a single movement.

execution.starting_position: Place two dumbbells on the floor, shoulder-width apart. Get into a push-up position with hands gripping the dumbbell handles, body forming a straight line from head to heels.
execution.setup_instructions: Use hex dumbbells, which sit flat and provide a stable base. Feet wider than hip-width increases stability and reduces anti-rotation demand.
steps: Step 1: Assume a high plank position with both hands on dumbbell handles.
Step 2: Brace the core and squeeze the glutes to prevent hip rotation.
Step 3: Row one dumbbell to the hip by driving the elbow straight up.
Step 4: Lower the dumbbell to the floor under control.
Step 5: Repeat on the other side. Each side counts as one rep.
execution.breathing_instructions: Exhale as you row, inhale as you return to the floor.
common_mistakes: Rotating the hips as you row — the hips must stay square
Using light dumbbells that allow too wide a foot stance, reducing the core challenge
Rushing the row, losing core position
safety_considerations: Use flat-bottomed hex dumbbells — round dumbbells on a hard floor are unstable and dangerous
Do not perform this exercise with wrist injuries or shoulder instability
execution.range_of_motion_guidance: Dumbbell stays on the floor at the start, pulled to hip level at the top while maintaining rigid plank.
coaching_cues: Make a T with your body when rowing
If your hips rotate, spread your feet wider
